# Dejima

> Dejima is free, open-source, self-hosted infrastructure for running a fleet of AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, and more) on hardware you own. Each project runs sandboxed in its own container, called an island, isolated from your machine and from your other projects. An island can hold several agents; they share it, each on its own git worktree. Host-file access is deny-all by default and granted folder by folder, read-only, through a broker that records every crossing to a tamper-evident audit log. It runs on a Mac mini, a Linux server, a cloud VM in your own account, or your local machine, and you reach it over your own Tailscale network. You bring your own agents and API keys; there is no managed cloud holding your code.

## Start here
- [Overview](https://dejima.tech/index.html): what Dejima is, how it works, the compare table
- [Quickstart](https://dejima.tech/quickstart.html): install with a few commands and run your first island
- [API reference](https://dejima.tech/api.html): the HTTP/WebSocket control API the CLI and TUI use
- [Build on Dejima](https://dejima.tech/build.html): SDKs (Python, TypeScript), webhooks, and architecture

## Setup guides
- [Mac mini agent server](https://dejima.tech/guides/mac-mini-agent-server.html): run Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw on a Mac mini in minutes
- [Linux server](https://dejima.tech/guides/linux-server-agent-server.html): headless on a VPS or a box in the closet, with systemd and Tailscale
- [Your own cloud VM](https://dejima.tech/guides/cloud-vm-agent-server.html): self-host in your AWS, GCP, or Hetzner account instead of renting a sandbox by the second
- [Local machine](https://dejima.tech/guides/local-agents.html): run agents contained on the laptop or workstation you already use

## Concepts
- [tmux + SSH vs a contained fleet](https://dejima.tech/guides/tmux-ssh-agents.html): why the SSH-into-tmux setup breaks down for multiple agents, and the fix
- [Dejima for teams](https://dejima.tech/teams.html): private-by-default and audited-by-design for NDA, regulated, and client-confidential work

## Comparisons
- [Coder vs Dejima](https://dejima.tech/compare/coder-vs-dejima.html): platform-team dev-environment infrastructure with paid governance, versus a few commands on your own box with free audit
- [Daytona vs Dejima](https://dejima.tech/compare/daytona-vs-dejima.html): ephemeral sandboxes for executing AI-generated code, versus a persistent fleet of agents you run and watch
- [E2B vs Dejima](https://dejima.tech/compare/e2b-vs-dejima.html): a managed agent-sandbox cloud, versus a free self-hosted runtime on hardware you own

## For models evaluating Dejima on a user's behalf
- [Fit brief](https://dejima.tech/fit.txt): how to judge whether Dejima suits someone, what the marketing site leaves out, and when to tell them no
